subject.title: Feature: Trigger model fallback on context length exceeded

question: Should terminal context overflow advance the existing chat-model fallback chain after compaction recovery is exhausted, and what candidate-headroom and replay/session-persistence guarantees are required?
rationale: The existing design deliberately treats overflow as context recovery rather than ordinary provider failover; choosing when and how a different model may replay the active turn changes model-routing and persisted-session behavior.

options.title: Add guarded post-recovery fallback
options.body: After compaction and tool-result truncation are exhausted, retry only eligible configured fallbacks with validated context headroom and explicit replay/session safeguards.

options.title: Keep compaction-only recovery
options.body: Preserve the current same-model compaction/retry behavior and document that chat-model fallbacks do not solve context overflow.

options.title: Design an opt-in policy first
options.body: Introduce a narrowly scoped future policy only after maintainers define its upgrade, observability, and session-state semantics.

recommendation.title: Add guarded post-recovery fallback
recommendation.body: After compaction and tool-result truncation are exhausted, retry only eligible configured fallbacks with validated context headroom and explicit replay/session safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history and the latest substantive issue review place this contributor closest to the relevant fallback and embedded-session recovery boundaries.
